newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian lek continues slide against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Albanian lek continues slide against dollar.

text.p: The Albanian lek continued to weaken against the U.S. dollar on Thursday as investors in alleged get-rich-quick schemes rushed to turn their returns into hard currency, foreign exchange dealers said.
The dollar has strengthened to 111.5 leks on Thursday, a two-year high, from 104 leks at the start of the year.

"There is big demand from citizens who are exchanging the payments they received from some of the schemes into dollars because they are afraid the lek could collapse if the schemes fold," a trader said.

Alleged pyramid schemes, which have mushroomed in Europe's poorest country, have drawn millions of dollars from depositors in Albania over the past years, taking vast sums of money outside the banking system and alarming world finance bodies.
One of the schemes has collapsed owing $13 million to depositors and two others have temporarily suspended payments to depositors.

The Savings Bank of Albania (SBA) said on Wednesday it had witnessed an influx of around $800,000 in hard currency into the bank in one day last week, a trend which had begun in mid-December and was growing increasingly visible.

"Depositors are receiving payments from firms (operating get-rich-quick schemes), turning them into dollars and trusting them to us. This has influenced the market," SBA general manager Bedri Collaku said.
A bank official said on Thursday the inflow was continuing and that the central bank was expected to intervene shortly. Nobody at the central bank was available for comment.
